work.text: Mucha designed posters for each successive Bernhardt play, beginning with a reprise of one of her early great successes, La Dame aux Camelias (September 1896), followed by Lorenzaccio (1896); Medea (1898); La Tosca (1898), and Hamlet (1899).
…Lorenzaccio, and the more forceful and effective Medee, these posters, as well as the costumes and scenery for the plays, which were likewise designed by Mucha, marked an epoch

moment.text: Bernhardt continued to employ Mucha to design her posters and expanded his work to include theatrical sets, programs, costumes, and jewellery props. His posters became icons of the Art Nouveau style. To earn more money, Bernhardt set aside a certain number of printed posters of each play to sell to collectors.

matters.text: In 1899, he collaborated with the jeweller Georges Fouquet to make a bracelet for Sarah Bernhardt in the form of a serpent, made of gold and enamel, similar to the costume jewellery Bernhardt had worn in Medea. According to Jiří Mucha, this bracelet was created to conceal Bernhardt's arthritic wrist.
